Aurelia · admin site · guideline · 11 November 2026

The Aurelia admin, module by module

What every part of the admin is for, what you see on it, what you can do, the rules behind it, who is allowed, and what the real backend will replace. Written for the people who will run Aurelia day to day.

23 screens · 21 modules in 8 groups All figures are sample data No admin login yet Staging build ac6f07d

Getting started

Where it is

  • Production: aureliaprod.vercel.app/admin
  • Staging: the staging site's /admin. New modules land here first.
  • The admin is part of the same app as the consumer site, not a separate system. Each site has its own copy.

How to get in

  • Enter the site password once, as for the consumer app. Ask the product owner; it is not written in any document.
  • There is no admin login yet. Anyone with the address and the password can open it (known gap P0).
  • The admin is built for desktop. It works on a phone, with wide tables scrolling sideways.

What the data is

  • Every number is generated sample data, made to look realistic, until the backend exists.
  • Edits (roles, suspensions, challenges, rules) apply in your browser for this visit only.
  • The top bar says Environment: staging · Data is mock so this is never a surprise.

The sidebar groups modules by the job they belong to. Click any name to jump to its chapter.

How the screens work

Page anatomy

  • Header: the module's name and one sentence on what it is for.
  • Headline cards: four to six figures, with a change against the previous period where it matters (green good, red bad; for costs and errors a rise is red).
  • Panels: charts and tables, each with a line saying what it shows.

Tables

  • Search box, filters, sortable columns, paging and Export CSV on every data table.
  • Wide tables scroll inside their panel; the page itself never scrolls sideways.
  • Rows with a name open that person or session.

Status colours

  • good active, published, on track
  • attention suspended, critical, overdue, at risk
  • Colour never carries meaning alone: every badge has its word.

Changes and safety

  • Destructive actions (delete, remove) always ask for confirmation first.
  • Privileged changes are meant to be written to the Audit log.
  • Health-related flags go to a person; nothing is acted on automatically.

Roles and permissions

Five staff roles. Super Admin always has everything; the others are edited on the Roles page. The matrix below is the current default. It takes effect once admin login exists.

Roleusers.readusers.writeusers.suspendsessions.readsessions.writemoderation.reviewmoderation.actionai.readai.configai.budgetcoins.readcoins.adjustroles.manageaudit.readsettings.write
Super AdminUnrestricted access, including roles and platform settings.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●
OperationsDay-to-day user and content operations. No AI config or role changes.●●●●●●●●··●··●·
ModeratorReviews reported sessions and community content only.●··●·●●········
AI EngineerOwns model configuration, prompts and spend limits.···●···●●●···●·
AnalystRead-only across the platform for reporting.●··●···●··●··●·
  • Users: users.read View users, users.write Edit users, users.suspend Suspend / ban users
  • Content: sessions.read View sessions, sessions.write Edit / unpublish sessions, moderation.review Review reports, moderation.action Take down content
  • AI: ai.read View AI monitoring, ai.config Change model / prompt config, ai.budget Set spend limits
  • Economy: coins.read View coin ledger, coins.adjust Grant / revoke coins
  • Platform: roles.manage Manage roles, audit.read View audit log, settings.write Change app settings

Several modules (revenue, payments, pricing, compliance, notifications, the study) have no permission of their own yet. Each chapter proposes one. Adding them is part of building admin login.

Overview

Overview

Dashboard

/admin StagingProduction

Platform health at a glance. It is the page to open first each morning: every figure links through to the module that owns it.

What you see

  • Six headline cards: users, published sessions, AI spend over 30 days, open reports, staff accounts, audit entries.
  • AI request volume over time.
  • Most played sessions in the published catalogue, by lifetime plays.
  • Needs attention: items from other modules that are waiting on someone.
  • Recent admin activity from the audit log.

What you can do

  • Click a card or a row to go to the module that owns it.

Rules to know

  • Figures are read-only here; changes happen in the owning module.
Permission
Any staff role (no permission of its own)
Backend (API contract)
Read model over the other modules; no endpoint of its own.

People

People

Users

/admin/users StagingProduction

Every account on the platform, consumers and staff. Role changes and suspensions take effect immediately.

What you see

  • Cards: total users (30-day change), active, paid plans with conversion, staff accounts.
  • A table with name and email, role, status (active / suspended / pending), plan, country, sessions, coins, joined and last active.

What you can do

  • Search by name or email; filter by status, plan, role and country; sort any column; export CSV.
  • Change a user's role from the dropdown in their row.
  • Suspend or reactivate a user.
  • Invite user: name, email and role, then Send invite.
  • Open a user to see their detail page.

Rules to know

  • Staff roles are the same accounts with a non-member role. The Roles page defines what each role can do.
  • There is no admin login yet, so today anyone with the address can make these changes (P0 gap).
Permission
users.read · users.write (role) · users.suspend
Backend (API contract)
GET/PATCH /admin/users, POST /admin/users/invite (API contract §7).

People

User detail

/admin/users/:id StagingProduction

One account's own history, filtered by user id (never by name): what they made, earned and did.

What you see

  • Header with role and status; cards for plan, coins, sessions created and last active.
  • Well-being outcome panel on staging: WHO-5, check-ins and resting heart rate for this user.
  • Sessions created, coin activity (earnings, spends, grants with balance after), and audit history (actions by and about this account).

What you can do

  • Go back to Users; open a session.

Rules to know

  • The outcome panel uses the same sample data as Well-being outcomes, so the two never disagree.
Permission
users.read
Backend (API contract)
GET /admin/users/{id}.

People

Well-being outcomes

/admin/outcomes StagingNot in production yet

How much each member's well-being has changed since they started, for Eugene's question about therapeutic improvement.

What you see

  • Cards: measured users (2+ WHO-5 scores), improved (+10 points or more), average change, follow-ups (latest WHO-5 at 28 or below).
  • Where people are (improved / steady / declined / too early) and average change by goal.
  • Every user: WHO-5 start and latest, change, check-ins first vs last, resting heart rate, outcome and follow-up flags.
  • How to read this.

What you can do

  • Search, filter by outcome, goal or follow-up, sort, export CSV, open a user.

Rules to know

  • WHO-5 changes of 10 points count as meaningful; 28 or below is a cue for a person to follow up, never Aurelia on its own.
  • Self-reported and observational: it is not proof Aurelia caused the change, and it is not a diagnosis.
  • The app does not ask WHO-5 yet; this runs on sample data.
Permission
Not defined yet (proposed: users.read + a health-data permission)
Backend (API contract)
Later: GET /admin/outcomes (needs WHO-5 in the app and Compliance wording; open item O21).

Experimentation

Experimentation

Feedback group · version 1

/admin/experimentation StagingNot in production yet

The 30-person, 8-week study of therapeutic outcomes, from the researcher's side: are we on track against the pass lines we set, and is the data good enough to judge?

What you see

  • A timeline of the eight weeks and what is collected when.
  • Cards: enrolled, active, WHO-5 +10 so far, data collected, follow-ups.
  • Success criteria with pass lines and status. Outcome lines read 'not yet' until week 8.
  • Well-being by cohort over time, a cohort table, and what the study can and cannot show.
  • Tabs: Participants (pseudonymous, filterable, CSV), What we collect (every measure, when, source, whether the app can collect it today), Data & safety (follow-ups, completeness, missing questionnaires).

What you can do

  • Switch between Version 1 and Version 2 at the top right.
  • Filter and export participants; open a participant.

Rules to know

  • Participants are P01–P30 only; names and contact details stay with the research team.
  • The study cannot prove Aurelia caused a change: there is no control group.
  • Sample data until the study runs on the backend.
Permission
Not defined yet (proposed: research lead role)
Backend (API contract)
GET /admin/studies/{id}, …/participants, …/quality (API contract §5.12).

Experimentation

Feedback group · version 2

/admin/experimentation/v2 StagingNot in production yet

The same study read the way Eugene framed it, 'solve and win them', and as the study team's week. Built for review beside version 1.

What you see

  • What is different from version 1 (expandable).
  • Wins: won (moved into the healthy band of their questionnaire), improving, steady, worse, started healthy. Per cohort: start-vs-now severity bands and every participant's status.
  • This week: a checklist of calls, missed questionnaires, what is due, low use and interviews.
  • Engagement: every participant's sessions per week as a heat strip, and WHO-5 change by how much people used it.

What you can do

  • Tick tasks as done (kept on the page only until the backend exists); show answered questionnaires.
  • Open any participant.

Rules to know

  • A win needs a meaningful change and arriving in the healthy band; 'started healthy' is shown apart because they had little to win.
  • Use and change moving together is an association, not proof.
Permission
Not defined yet (proposed: research lead role)
Backend (API contract)
Same endpoints as version 1.

Intelligence

Intelligence

AI monitoring

/admin/ai StagingProduction

Cost, latency, reliability, output quality and safety for every model call. Quality scores come from an LLM-as-judge rubric on a sampled slice of traffic.

What you see

  • Cards: requests, p95 latency, error rate, refusal rate, average judge score.
  • Daily spend by model, latency percentiles, a model breakdown (requests, tokens, cost, p50/p95, errors).
  • Output quality, safety and guardrails, and request traces.

What you can do

  • Change the time window; read traces.

Rules to know

  • Figures are sample data. In the API contract each AI route (cockpit reply, proposals, build, safety…) reports here.
Permission
ai.read
Backend (API contract)
GET /admin/ai/metrics, /admin/ai/traces/{id}.

Intelligence

Cockpit rules

/admin/cockpit-rules StagingProduction

The reply engine behind every chat today: a keyword matcher, not a model. The first rule whose pattern matches wins.

What you see

  • Cards: rules, how many propose a brief, how many produce a new cut, the fallback.
  • Every rule with its trigger pattern, reply text and prompts.

What you can do

  • Edit a rule: trigger pattern, reply text, prompts offered instead of an answer.
  • Edit the fallback reply.

Rules to know

  • Order is priority: specific rules before general ones.
  • When real AI arrives, this page becomes AI policies: a versioned prompt, model and effort per AI route, with draft and publish.
Permission
ai.config
Backend (API contract)
GET/PUT /admin/ai/policies/{route}.

Platform

Platform

Compliance & privacy

/admin/compliance StagingProduction

Aurelia processes mood, sleep and voice data, which is special-category data under GDPR Art. 9. Each purpose is consented separately, and subject requests carry a statutory clock.

What you see

  • Cards: open requests, overdue, deletion requests, special-category opt-in.
  • Data subject requests with the right, regime, owner and statutory due date; the consent ledger; the retention schedule.

What you can do

  • Search, filter and export requests.

Rules to know

  • Overdue requests are a legal risk, not a backlog item.
Permission
Not defined yet (proposed: compliance officer)
Backend (API contract)
GET /admin/compliance/requests.

Platform

Signal sources

/admin/signal-sources StagingProduction

The integrations Progress (My Wellness) can read, consent-gated per source. The 'Reads' text is the exact text a member agrees to.

What you see

  • Cards: sources, on by default.
  • Each source with its group, icon and what Aurelia reads.

What you can do

  • Add a source, edit it (name, group, icon, what it reads) or remove it with a confirmation.

Rules to know

  • Changing the Reads text changes a consent record: a new version should ask users again.
Permission
Not defined yet (proposed: settings.write)
Backend (API contract)
CRUD /admin/signal-sources.

No module matches that search.

Known gaps and roadmap

Gaps today

  • No admin login (P0): every module is reachable by address. Fixed by SSO with staff roles.
  • Sample data everywhere: nothing is read from a database yet.
  • Edits do not persist beyond the visit.
  • The study needs questionnaires in the app before week 0.

What the backend adds (API contract)

  • P0: accounts, persistence, admin login and the audit log.
  • P1: AI monitoring and AI policies fed by real model calls.
  • P3: payments, coins and challenges on real data.
  • P4: every admin module on real data, plus the outcomes module once WHO-5 is in the app.

Glossary

WHO-5A five-question well-being index from 0 to 100. A change of 10 points is meaningful; 28 or below is a cue for a person to follow up.
Cohort measureThe validated questionnaire for a participant's own issue: ISI (sleep), GAD-7 (anxiety), PROMIS Cognitive Function (fog, focus), PROMIS Fatigue (energy), PSS-10 (stress).
WinIn the study's version 2: moving from the problem range into the healthy band of the cohort measure.
AdherenceThe share of weeks with three or more sessions played.
Cut / versionA built version of a session (v1.0, v1.1 …). Live is what listeners get; current is what the owner edits.
MRR / NRR / ARPU / LTVMonthly recurring revenue; net revenue retention; average revenue per user; lifetime value.
DunningRetrying failed card payments before a subscription lapses.
DSARA data subject request under GDPR (access, deletion, correction), with a statutory deadline.
LLM-as-judgeA model scoring a sample of AI outputs against a rubric, shown in AI monitoring.
Sample dataRealistic generated figures used until the backend exists. Never quote them as results.
